allocation: one per occupied stratum, then largest proportional deficit; lexical ties
baseline_policy: comparison only; never candidates or production recommendations
estimator: sum_h (N_h/N) * mean(selected grades in h); baselines use raw mean
features: Benchmark metadata input_tokens and canonical source-URL counts; empirical midrank thirds. Metadata-only candidate crosses length and document count; historical candidate crosses length and reference pass count. Target grades and model usage excluded before fitting.
implementation_hash_policy: SHA256 of source bytes after CRLF-to-LF normalization
interval_policy: equal-tail hypergeometric inversion with exact integer tail comparisons; Bonferroni across strata and both directional discordances for paired differences; no intervals for deterministic top-k except at census
limitations: Only three historical models; each fold fits on two. This is not proof for a fourth model.
Ordering uses the same subset within a fold, but includes two in-sample reference models.
Held-out scores alone measure transfer; no ranking combines scores from different subsets.
Seed dispersion measures selection sensitivity on fixed grades, not generation uncertainty.
No customer threshold or production operating point is fitted; thresholds are user inputs.
Exact intervals assume uniform within-stratum sampling; fixed hash priorities approximate it.
Intervals concern fixed grades, not future tasks, generation noise, or unseen model families.
Coverage is per fixed run, not simultaneous over methods, ratios, seeds, or searches.
Pair transfer excludes both compared models; only one reference remains in this panel.
Easiest/hardest comparisons have no intervals except when the entire pool is observed.
Index correspondence across models is assumed from the supplied benchmark contract.
This offline experiment does not satisfy the later evalscope integration requirement.
Questions and URLs are available, but these candidates do not establish semantic/topic coverage.
Length uses shared benchmark input_tokens, not model-dependent model_output.usage.
Repeated document sets create dependence for future-task inference; design intervals concern only this fixed pool.
Document-count and length coverage do not guarantee coverage of all source sets at small budgets.
Only one judge review per answer; judge noise and systematic judge bias are not identifiable.
Judge flip budgets are conditional sensitivity assumptions, not estimated noise rates or confidence intervals.
Sampling intervals collapse at census, but unmeasured judge uncertainty does not.
Input-token totals are a cost proxy; latency, output tokens, cache reuse and judge cost are not measured.
ordering_policy: common subset per fold; reference-assisted; ties within 1e-12
